clue.text: Good-natured deer transported for Spooner

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the phrase must be said as he would say it

blocks.note: a hind is a female deer; it trades its opening sound with the next word
transported means carried off, as in a cart; it takes the H sound in exchange for its K sound

explanation.surface: A gentle deer being moved somewhere, with the Reverend's name tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: HIND CARTED, with the opening sounds exchanged, becomes KIND HEARTED. 'Good-natured deer' reads as one phrase, but the adjective is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone kind-hearted has a warm, generous disposition, which is what being good-natured means.

clue.text: Realm of prince and princess invaded by Chinese dynasts

indicators.note: an invaded country has an army inside its borders, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Kate, the Princess of Wales
the Han were a ruling Chinese dynasty

explanation.surface: A royal couple's kingdom overrun by imperial Chinese rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prince and princess' looks like a pair, but the prince belongs to the definition and 'and' only joins it to the wordplay. The princess is the current Princess of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A khan is a ruler or prince in Central Asia, and the territory a khan governs is called a khanate.

clue.text: Head north with unopened piece of cake

indicators.note: something not opened has lost its opening, so the first letter is gone

blocks.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north
a doddle is British slang for an easy task
without its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone sets off northwards carrying a slice of cake that has not been cut into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head north' reads as an instruction to travel, but Head is the definition. A doddle is British slang for something very easy, as is 'a piece of cake'.
explanation.definitionFit: Noddle is an old informal British word for the head, often used of someone's brain or wits.

clue.text: Extremely huffy and cross overturning lubricants for nautical devices

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters are kept
something overturned is flipped over, so in this down entry the letters run upwards

blocks.note: the first and last letters
to ford a river is to cross it
oils are used to lubricate machinery

explanation.surface: A very irritable, angry person knocking over the oil cans meant for boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a second word for angry beside huffy, but it is the verb, as in crossing a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrofoils are wing-like fins that lift a boat's hull clear of the water, or the fast boats fitted with them.

clue.text: Top club in which leader’s demoted

indicators.note: a leader demoted loses the top position, so the opening letter comes off the front
the letter that left the front is placed in the remaining letters, lower down this down entry

blocks.note: a mace is a heavy spiked club
without its first letter
the first letter of the club word, now set further down

explanation.surface: At the best club in town, the boss has been knocked down a peg.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, demoting a letter moves it lower: the M of MACE drops two places to give ACME.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the highest point or peak of achievement, so it is a noun synonym for the top.

clue.text: Dancing function off

blocks.note: tan is the short name of the tangent, a trigonometric function
to be off is to be leaving

explanation.surface: A dance function has been called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancing function' reads as a ball or dance party; the maths sense of function is the one wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To tango is to perform a particular Argentine dance, so tangoing is one specific form of dancing.

clue.text: Figure it’s a month since November

blocks.note: DEC is the calendar abbreviation for December
since, as in 'long since', means ago
November is N in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone works out that a month has passed since November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a verb meaning reckon, but it is a noun, a geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A decagon is a ten-sided polygon, and polygons are plane figures in geometry.

clue.text: Labelled and brought forth clothes

indicators.note: to clothe is to wrap around, so one piece is dressed around another

blocks.note: to breed young is to bring them forth
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fashion house tagged its garments and launched them on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' reads as the garments themselves, but it is a verb meaning dresses, wrapping one piece around the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To brand something is to mark it with a name or logo, so a branded item has been labelled.

clue.text: Cook conveying rats to market-town

indicators.note: to convey is to carry, and what is carried is held within

blocks.note: to bake is to cook in an oven
to rat on someone is to inform, and an informer sings to the police

explanation.surface: A chef carts a load of rats off to the local market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rats' looks like vermin, but it is the verb: to rat is to grass, which in slang is to sing. BASINGSTOKE is a market town in Hampshire, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Basingstoke grew up as a town with a chartered weekly market, so it is one example of the category.

clue.text: Messing with this bully, she and I might become arch-enemies

indicators.note: messing with something throws it into disorder, so the combined letters are scrambled
the clue says what, joined to extra letters, would rearrange into a phrase, so those extras must be taken back off

blocks.note: the full set of letters the combined anagram must make
taken as written; these letters come off the full set

explanation.surface: Two people warn that tangling with a playground bully will turn them into bitter foes.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus SHE and I shuffle to ARCHENEMIES. 'This bully' is the definition, pointed at by 'this'.
explanation.definitionFit: A menacer is someone who threatens or intimidates others, which is exactly what a bully does.

clue.text: Call for support in upcoming year after Republican joining forces with core of Democrats

indicators.note: the core of something is its centre, so only the middle letter is kept
coming up in a down entry means reading from the bottom upwards
after places the first-named piece at the end, behind everything that follows it in the clue

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for Republican
allying is forming an alliance, joining forces
the fifth of nine letters
YR is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: An American election message: a Republican teaming up with Democrats next year to drum up support.
explanation.walkthrough: The year is named first but goes last, upside down, after the other three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A rallying cry is a slogan or shout used to gather people behind a cause, an appeal for backing.

clue.text: Stop one riding horse

blocks.note: to stall is to stop or come to a halt
I is the Roman numeral for one
a rider is on a mount

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt someone who is out on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One riding' looks like a rider, but it splits into the numeral and a word for being astride something.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an adult male horse kept uncastrated, often for breeding, so it is one kind of horse.

clue.text: Asian person immersed in Pokémon Gold

indicators.note: something immersed sits wholly inside a liquid, so the letters lie within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run consecutively across the end of the first word and into the second

explanation.surface: Someone from Asia absorbed in playing the video game Pokémon Gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The accent on the é is ignored; it is just an E for the grid, and the hidden letters start after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mongol is a native of Mongolia or a member of its people, who live in Central and East Asia.

clue.text: Necessary for building muscles, maintaining routine, rogue lifted

indicators.note: to maintain is to keep and hold, so one piece holds the others
lifted in a down entry means raised so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: lats are the latissimus dorsi, the broad back muscles
a rut is a dull fixed routine
a cur is a scoundrel or rogue

explanation.surface: A gym regime: build muscle by sticking to a routine, as a rogue lifts weights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building muscles' reads as bodybuilding, but building is the construction sense. The muscles hold the routine and the rogue, then the whole lot is turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Structural describes parts that hold a building up, the elements it cannot stand without.

clue.text: Miss irritated getting led away

indicators.note: something sent away is no longer present, so those letters leave the word

blocks.note: to needle someone is to irritate them
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A young woman grows annoyed at being escorted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a title for a young woman, but it is the verb, as in missing someone you love.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss someone or something is to feel its absence and want it back, a close synonym for requiring it.

clue.text: Siren snubbed pamper party in LA

indicators.note: a snub nose is short and turned up, so to snub here is to cut off the end

blocks.note: a hooter is a siren or horn
without its last letter
to nanny is to fuss over and pamper

explanation.surface: A seductive woman, cold-shouldered, throws a pampering party in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snubbed' looks like rejected socially; here it means docked at the end, as in a snub nose. LA stands for the American setting, since the word is chiefly American.
explanation.definitionFit: A hootenanny is an informal American gathering with folk music and dancing, a kind of party.

clue.text: Worker about to be lost in corporate reshuffling

indicators.note: what is lost from something is no longer in it, so those letters are dropped
reshuffling a pack puts the cards in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
taken as written

explanation.surface: An employee is about to lose their job in a company restructuring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to be lost' reads as imminent redundancy, but 'about' is the abbreviation for circa that must come out before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: An operator is someone who works a machine or runs a process, a general word for a worker.

clue.text: Returning drink coasters with duff place for collection

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does
drinks coasters are table mats
duff and bum are both British slang for the backside

explanation.surface: Bringing back beer mats with a useless spot to keep them all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink coasters' looks like one phrase, but the drink is a verb. 'Duff' reads as an adjective meaning useless; here it is the British slang noun for the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamp album is a book where a philatelist keeps and displays a collection of postage stamps.

clue.text: Checked treads regularly beneath car

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter, keeping the odd positions
in a down entry, beneath means placed lower, so the first-named piece goes second

blocks.note: Audi is a German make of car
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A mechanic regularly inspected the tyre treads under a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checked treads' reads as a tyre inspection; 'Checked' is the definition and the treads are only letter fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To audit accounts or records is to inspect them officially, so audited means formally examined.

clue.text: Get close after cycling

indicators.note: a cycle goes round and round, so a letter travels from the front to the back

blocks.note: close by means near

explanation.surface: Pull up close behind someone on a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get close' reads as a single phrase, but 'Get' stands alone as the definition. The N goes round from front to back.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn money or a reward is to receive or obtain it, the commonest sense of the verb get.

clue.text: Soldier perhaps on island, untrained, upset and non-violent

indicators.note: to upset is to tip over, and in a down entry tipped letters read upwards

blocks.note: a soldier ant is one kind of ant; perhaps marks the example
I is the abbreviation for island
a raw recruit is untrained

explanation.surface: An untrained soldier posted to an island turns against fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' wants to be a military recruit, but it is the insect: soldier ants are a caste of ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Being antiwar means opposing armed conflict, so the word is a fair match for pacifist or non-violent.

clue.text: Chunky person in scrum times hooks

indicators.note: to hook something is to catch and hold it, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: times, as in multiplication, is by: three by four
a lock is a second-row forward in a rugby scrum

explanation.surface: A beefy rugby forward in the scrum sometimes wins the ball for the hooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooks' suggests the rugby hooker in the scrum, but it is the containment verb. A lock is a rugby union position in the scrum's second row.
explanation.definitionFit: Chunky and blocky both describe something thick, solid and squarely built.

clue.text: What comes from those demanding sorts

blocks.note: first meaning: commands issued by people who insist on things
second meaning: kinds or classes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Demanding sorts' reads as one phrase for bossy people; split it, and sorts is a noun meaning kinds.
explanation.definitionFit: Commands are what demanding people give, and in biology or society an order is a rank or class of things.

clue.text: Sorry to lose lead before crossing line, as runner might be

indicators.note: losing the lead means losing the front position, so the first letter goes
to cross something is to span it, so one piece straddles the other

blocks.note: a sorry sight is a pathetic one
without its first letter
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A runner, sadly overtaken just before the finishing line, is sorry to lose the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: The racing surface makes 'line' the finishing line and 'lead' first place; both are wordplay, not part of the race.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner is typically fit, strong and sporty, which is what athletic describes; the phrase works as an adjective.

clue.text: Maybe dogs tramp raised

indicators.note: raised in a down entry means lifted so the letters read from the bottom up

blocks.note: to tramp is to step heavily

explanation.surface: Perhaps a homeless wanderer brought up a few dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a vagrant, but it is the verb meaning to walk heavily. 'Maybe' marks dogs as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogs are one common kind of animal kept at home for company, so they are an example of the category.

clue.text: Style of space headgear covering Tim’s head

indicators.note: a cover goes over and around something, so one piece wraps the other
the head of a word is its top, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em wide
tile is old British slang for a hat
the opening letter

explanation.surface: Tim models a space helmet, a sci-fi fashion statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Style' looks like a noun for fashion, but it is the verb meaning to give a name or title to. 'Space headgear' suggests a helmet; the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To style someone as something is to designate them by that name or title, which is what entitle means in its older sense.

clue.text: People with word of affirmation for course

blocks.note: a race is a people sharing ancestry
W is the abbreviation for word
ay, or aye, is an old word for yes

explanation.surface: A group of people saying yes to a plan, or a course of action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Word of affirmation' reads as one phrase meaning yes; it splits into the abbreviation for word and the yes itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A raceway is a track built for racing cars, horses or other contests, which is a racecourse.

clue.text: Assembled parts ready to house large missile launcher

indicators.note: assembled means put together in a new form, so the letters are rearranged
to house something is to give it a home inside, so one piece goes within

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Components put together, ready to accommodate a big rocket on its launch pad.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says a weapons system; the definition is playful, since darts are small missiles thrown by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A darts player throws small pointed projectiles at a board, so the setter can fairly call them a launcher of missiles.
